gloss: triangular bandage; arm sling; (kitchen) triangular head scarf

definitions.explanation: A triangular cloth used in first aid to immobilize an injured arm or support a wound. A standard item in school and workplace first-aid kits.

definitions.gloss: triangular head scarf (worn in cooking class)
definitions.explanation: A triangular cloth worn over the hair to keep it out of food. Standard equipment for elementary school cooking classes and school lunch duty.

examples.japanese: {腕|うで}を{三角巾|さんかくきん}で{吊|つ}った。
examples.english: I put my arm in a sling.

examples.japanese: {救急箱|きゅうきゅうばこ}には{三角巾|さんかくきん}が{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: There is a triangular bandage in the first-aid kit.

examples.japanese: {骨折|こっせつ}した{右手|みぎて}を{三角巾|さんかくきん}で{固定|こてい}してもらった。
examples.english: They put my fractured right hand in a sling to immobilize it.

examples.japanese: {給食|きゅうしょく}{当番|とうばん}は{三角巾|さんかくきん}をつける。
examples.english: Students on school-lunch duty wear a head scarf.

examples.japanese: {調理|ちょうり}{実習|じっしゅう}では{三角巾|さんかくきん}とエプロンを{着用|ちゃくよう}する。
examples.english: In cooking class, we wear a head scarf and an apron.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}が{白|しろ}い{三角巾|さんかくきん}を{頭|あたま}に{巻|ま}いて{台所|だいどころ}に{立|た}っていた。
examples.english: My mother was standing in the kitchen with a white head scarf wrapped around her hair.

notes:
Compound of {三角|さんかく} (triangle) + {巾|きん} (cloth). The same shaped cloth is used for two unrelated purposes: emergency first aid and keeping hair out of food.

SENSE 1 — FIRST AID:
- An essential item in any {救急箱|きゅうきゅうばこ} (first-aid kit).
- Used to make an arm sling, secure a splint, or cover a wound.

SENSE 2 — KITCHEN:
- Standard kit for {給食|きゅうしょく}{当番|とうばん} (school-lunch duty) and {調理|ちょうり}{実習|じっしゅう} (cooking class), worn together with an apron.
- Often the first thing a Japanese child learns to wear in a domestic kitchen setting.
